cc-http.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-http.quote: HTTP servers are the recommended option for connecting to remote MCP servers.

cc-stdio.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-stdio.quote: Stdio servers run as local processes on your machine. They’re ideal for tools that need direct system access or custom scripts.

cc-dashdash.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-dashdash.quote: For stdio servers, the -- (double dash) separates Claude’s own options, such as --transport, --env, and --scope, from the command and arguments that run the server. Everything after -- is passed to the server untouched.

local-npx.title: Connect to local MCP servers
local-npx.quote: "command": "npx": Uses Node.js’s npx tool to run the server "-y": Automatically confirms the installation of the server package

local-node.title: Connect to local MCP servers
local-node.quote: The Filesystem Server and many other MCP servers require Node.js to run.

local-dirs.title: Connect to local MCP servers
local-dirs.quote: The paths listed in the args array specify which directories the Filesystem Server can access.

cc-env-order.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-env-order.quote: --env accepts multiple KEY=value pairs. If the server name comes directly after --env, the CLI reads the name as another pair and rejects it

cc-manage.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-manage.quote: # List all configured servers claude mcp list # Get details for a specific server claude mcp get notion # Remove a server claude mcp remove notion # (within Claude Code) Check server status /mcp

cc-status.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-status.quote: claude mcp list shows a health status next to each server it lists, such as ✔ Connected,! Needs authentication, or ✘ Failed to connect.

cc-scopes.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-scopes.quote: MCP servers can be configured at three scopes. The scope you choose controls which projects the server loads in and whether the configuration is shared with your team. Administrators can also deploy or provide servers for every user via managed configuration. Scope Loads in Shared with team Stored in Local Current project only No ~/.claude.json Project Current project only Yes, via version control .mcp.json in project root User All your projects No ~/.claude.json

cc-local.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-local.quote: Local scope is the default. A local-scoped server loads only in the project where you added it and stays private to you.

cc-project.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-project.quote: Project-scoped servers enable team collaboration by storing configurations in a .mcp.json file at your project’s root directory.

cc-notype.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-notype.quote: A JSON entry that has a url but no type is a configuration error, because Claude Code reads an entry with no type as a stdio server. Claude Code skips that server

cc-precedence.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-precedence.quote: When the same server is defined in more than one place, Claude Code connects to it once, using the definition from the highest-precedence source. The entire server entry from that source is used; fields are not merged across scopes. Local scope Project scope User scope

cc-env-syntax.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-env-syntax.quote: Supported syntax ${VAR}: expands to the value of environment variable VAR ${VAR:-default}: expands to VAR if set, otherwise uses default

cc-env-why.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-env-why.quote: Claude Code supports environment variable expansion in .mcp.json files, allowing teams to share configurations while maintaining flexibility for machine-specific paths and sensitive values like API keys.

cc-env-unset.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-env-unset.quote: If a referenced environment variable isn’t set and has no default value, the config still loads: Claude Code reports a missing-variable warning for that server in claude mcp list output and uses the unexpanded ${VAR} text as-is.

cc-verify.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-verify.quote: Verify you trust each server before connecting it. Servers that fetch external content can expose you to prompt injection risk.

hc-untrusted2.title: Handle tool calls
hc-untrusted2.quote: Tool results often carry content from sources outside your control: web pages, inbound email, user uploads, third-party APIs. Treat that content as untrusted: an attacker who can influence it may embed instructions that try to redirect Claude (indirect prompt injection).

sec-local.title: Security Best Practices
sec-local.quote: Local MCP servers are binaries that are downloaded and executed on the same machine as the MCP client.

local-perms.title: Connect to local MCP servers
local-perms.quote: The server runs with your user account permissions, so it can perform any file operations you can perform manually.

sec-startup.title: Security Best Practices
sec-startup.quote: An attacker includes a malicious “startup” command in a client configuration

sec-patterns.title: Security Best Practices
sec-patterns.quote: Highlight potentially dangerous command patterns (e.g., commands containing sudo, rm -rf, network operations, file system access outside expected directories)

spec-safety.title: MCP specification
spec-safety.quote: Tools represent arbitrary code execution and must be treated with appropriate caution. In particular, descriptions of tool behavior such as annotations should be considered untrusted, unless obtained from a trusted server.

cc-readonly.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-readonly.quote: Use a read-only database user in the connection string so the queries Claude runs can’t modify data

cc-approve.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-approve.quote: For security reasons, Claude Code prompts for approval in interactive sessions before using project-scoped servers from .mcp.json files.

cc-clone.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-clone.quote: A cloned repository can’t approve its own servers: enableAllProjectMcpServers or enabledMcpjsonServers committed to the project’s .claude/settings.json is ignored in an untrusted folder

cc-noprompt.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-noprompt.quote: In claude -p runs, Agent SDK sessions, and cloud sessions, Claude Code can’t show that prompt: it loads project-scoped servers without asking.

perm-mcp.title: Configure permissions
perm-mcp.quote: MCP rules use the server name as configured in Claude Code, optionally followed by the name of a tool from that server. mcp__puppeteer matches any tool provided by the puppeteer server mcp__puppeteer__* uses wildcard syntax and also matches all tools from the puppeteer server mcp__puppeteer__puppeteer_navigate matches the puppeteer_navigate tool provided by the puppeteer server

cc-nodash.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-nodash.quote: Without --, Claude Code would try to parse the server’s flags, like --port above, as its own options.

cc-env-locations.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-env-locations.quote: Environment variables can be expanded in: command: the server executable path args: command-line arguments env: environment variables passed to the server

cc-bearer.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-bearer.quote: # Example with Bearer token claude mcp add --transport http secure-api https://api.example.com/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer your-token"

mdn-https.title: HTTPS, MDN Web Docs
mdn-https.quote: HTTPS (HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure) is an encrypted version of the HTTP protocol. It uses TLS to encrypt all communication between a client and a server.

local-start.title: Connect to local MCP servers
local-start.quote: The process involves configuring Claude Desktop to automatically start the Filesystem Server whenever you launch the application.

perm-prompts.title: Configure permissions
perm-prompts.quote: On most permission prompts, including Bash, PowerShell, file, and MCP tool prompts

perm-files.title: Configure permissions
perm-files.quote: You can view and manage Claude Code’s tool permissions with /permissions. The dialog lists all permission rules and the settings.json file each rule comes from.

perm-user.title: Configure permissions
perm-user.quote: To apply permission rules across all your projects, add them to your user settings instead: ~/.claude/settings.json

perm-deny.title: Configure permissions
perm-deny.quote: This configuration denies every MCP tool: { "permissions": { "deny": ["mcp__*"] } }

cc-env-flag.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-env-flag.quote: claude mcp add --env KEY=value --transport stdio myserver -- python server.py --port 8080 → runs python server.py --port 8080 with KEY=value in environment

cc-scope-flag.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-scope-flag.quote: Each command writes to local scope unless you add --scope project or --scope user.

perm-kinds.title: Configure permissions
perm-kinds.quote: Allow rules let Claude Code use the specified tool without manual approval. Ask rules prompt for confirmation whenever Claude Code tries to use the specified tool. Deny rules prevent Claude Code from using the specified tool.

perm-order.title: Configure permissions
perm-order.quote: Rules are evaluated in order: deny, then ask, then allow. The first match in that order determines the outcome

cc-trust.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
cc-trust.quote: As of v2.1.196, claude mcp list and claude mcp get read .mcp.json approvals only from settings files that aren’t checked into the repository until you trust the workspace by running claude in it and accepting the workspace trust dialog.

perm-glob.title: Configure permissions
perm-glob.quote: Deny and ask rules also accept glob patterns in the tool-name position. The pattern must match the full tool name: "*" matches every tool, and "mcp__*" matches every MCP tool across all servers.

perm-allow-glob.title: Configure permissions
perm-allow-glob.quote: Allow rules accept tool-name globs only after a literal mcp__<server>__ prefix. The server segment must be glob-free so the rule names a specific server you configured. mcp__puppeteer__* matches every tool from the puppeteer server, and mcp__github__get_* matches its get_ tools. An unanchored allow glob such as "*", "B*", or "mcp__*" is skipped with a warning and doesn’t auto-approve anything.
